problem:
Problem description
- There is a single promotional planning horizon $$\mathcal{T}$$ over which the store decides how many promotional packages to sell.
- The store has a set of legacy item types $$\mathcal{I}$$ with available starting stock given by the inventory vector $$u_i$$ for each item $$i \in \mathcal{I}$$.
- The store offers a set of promotional package types $$\mathcal{P}$$. Each package type $$p \in \mathcal{P}$$ uses known quantities of the underlying items, recorded by the composition matrix $$a_{i,p}$$.
- Each package type $$p \in \mathcal{P}$$ generates revenue $$r_p$$ per unit sold.
- The promotion may also include optional external demand limits $$d_p$$ and optional unit cost information $$c_p$$ if such data are provided; the original instance is revenue-driven and does not provide these additional values.
- The store must decide the number of units $$x_p$$ to sell for each package type $$p \in \mathcal{P}$$.
- Each package type has a minimum required sales level $$\ell_p$$ that must be met during the promotion.
- Total item usage across all sold packages must not exceed the available stock of each item.
- Sales quantities must be whole numbers and cannot be negative.
- The planning goal is to maximize total promotional revenue.
- A solution is represented by:
  - $$x_p$$: the number of units of package type $$p$$ sold during $$\mathcal{T}$$.
  - $$z$$: the total revenue obtained from the selected sales plan.

Input Format
{
  "time_horizon": "Single promotional horizon $$\mathcal{T}$$.",
  "items": "List of item identifiers, size $$|\mathcal{I}|$$.",
  "packages": "List of package identifiers, size $$|\mathcal{P}|$$.",
  "inventory": "Vector $$u_i$$ of available units for each item $$i \in \mathcal{I}$$, length $$|\mathcal{I}|$$.",
  "composition": "Matrix $$a_{i,p}$$ giving the units of item $$i$$ consumed by one unit of package $$p$$, shape $$|\mathcal{I}| \times |\mathcal{P}|$$.",
  "price": "Vector $$r_p$$ of revenue per unit sold for each package $$p \in \mathcal{P}$$, length $$|\mathcal{P}|$$.",
  "minimum_sales": "Vector $$\ell_p$$ of minimum required sales for each package $$p \in \mathcal{P}$$, length $$|\mathcal{P}|$$.",
  "demand": "Optional vector $$d_p$$ of external demand limits for each package $$p \in \mathcal{P}$$, length $$|\mathcal{P}|$$.",
  "unit_cost": "Optional vector $$c_p$$ of unit costs for each package $$p \in \mathcal{P}$$, length $$|\mathcal{P}|$$."
}

Output Format
{
  "sales_plan": "Vector $$x_p$$ of optimal nonnegative integer sales quantities for each package $$p \in \mathcal{P}$$, length $$|\mathcal{P}|$$.",
  "total_revenue": "Scalar $$z$$ equal to the maximum achievable promotional revenue."
}

Example(s)

Input 1
{
  "time_horizon": 1,
  "items": ["shirts", "pants"],
  "packages": ["A", "B"],
  "inventory": [200, 100],
  "composition": [
    [1, 3],
    [2, 1]
  ],
  "price": [30, 50],
  "minimum_sales": [20, 10]
}

parameters.name: starting_inventory
parameters.description: Available starting inventory of each legacy item type

parameters.name: item_consumption
parameters.description: Quantity of each item consumed by one unit of each package type

parameters.name: revenue_per_unit
parameters.description: Revenue earned per unit sold of each package type

parameters.name: minimum_sales_level
parameters.description: Minimum required sales level for each package type

parameters.name: optional_demand_limit
parameters.description: Optional external demand limit for each package type

parameters.name: optional_unit_cost
parameters.description: Optional unit cost for each package type

variables.name: sales_quantity
variables.description: Number of units sold for each package type during the planning horizon

variables.name: total_revenue
variables.description: Total revenue obtained from the sales plan

constraints.name: inventory_capacity
constraints.description: Total item consumption across all sold packages must not exceed starting inventory for each item.

constraints.name: revenue_definition
constraints.description: Define total revenue as the sum of per-unit revenues across all sold packages.

constraints.name: revenue_scalar_definition
constraints.description: The scalar total revenue variable equals the revenue from the sales plan.

constraints.name: sales_domain_and_minimum_bounds
constraints.description: Each package sales quantity must be an integer no less than its minimum required sales level.

objectives.name: total_promotional_revenue_maximization
objectives.description: Maximize total promotional revenue over the planning horizon

final_objective.description: Maximize total promotional revenue over the planning horizon; the scalar revenue variable is defined by the sales quantities and per-unit revenues.
